claims.text: DFT calculations can effectively control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
DFT can predict the formation energies of constituent phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
DFT can predict the stability of constituent phases in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
The as-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEA initially has a disordered FCC structure.
The proposed DFT calculation uses a plane-wave basis set and the PBE exchange-correlation functional.
The proposed calculations are performed at 0 K with a 500 eV plane-wave cutoff.
DFT-derived formation energies can be used to construct phase-stability information relevant to phase evolution.
Ab initio calculations can predict phase stability and transformation pathways in this alloy system.
DFT-guided phase control will reduce the B2-phase volume fraction by 20% relative to the as-cast baseline.
The B2-phase volume fraction can be assessed by X-ray diffraction.
The predicted B2-phase volume fraction has an uncertainty of ±5%.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described simply as disordered FCC, but the outcome requires a baseline B2-phase volume fraction. The hypothesis does not clarify whether the baseline is multiphase or how B2 is present in the stated FCC initial state.
The stated prediction boundary is ±5%, whereas falsification is triggered only outside a 10% interval; the two acceptance tolerances are inconsistent or insufficiently distinguished.
